reviews.title: Budget Build Dream Case
reviews.comment:
In short, you won’t find better looking and better quality for this price.
For the overall compact size of the case it has great features. Comes with 3 pre installed argb fans which are quite nice. Plenty of front panel IO. The ease to build in for me was very easy. I would highly recommend this for an ITX or mATX build. For my build I installed two reverse airflow fans in the bottom and a 120mm AIO (for the nostalgia) and kept the two others in the top of the case. Running an I7 and 5700XT temps on GPU stay under 55 and CPU has never reached 68. (Don't judge my one stick of ram it was a placeholder while my kit arrived) As a side note DarkFlash has a great after sales and customer service team.
reviews.author: Lazaro Gonzalez

reviews.title: Amazing case
reviews.comment:
It surprises me to see the negative reviews this case has.  I've built over 90 computers as a side project flipping for fun.  This is one of the best cases I've ever used.
Airflow:  Yes, the top fans are mounted to blow air up.  They're easy to flip to draw air in.  Then you get as much air flow as any normal front mounted.
Quality:  The metal on this case is relatively thick and doesn't flex, especially compared to other budget or even high-end cases.  The glass panels fit together nicely.  Yes, the metal side panel is a little tricky to get on, but it's not bad.  The rounded edges on top look nice and make this case stand out some in a good way.  The cover on the case back for covering the PCEI ports is on hinges, which is convenient and looks nice.  The holes on the floor of the case between the main chamber and PSU provide for additional airflow.  The power button feels solid and is nice to press.
Cable routing:  There is plenty of space to route cables in the back and under the case, even with non-modular PSUs.  This was easy.  The holes for cable routing are nicely placed and make sense.
Fans:  They are amazing--quiet and beautiful.  They have a different, round profile on the side that makes them look premium.
Yes, the cabling is black.  So are the cables on most PSUs.  If you really want, you can get cable extensions and hide the cabling behind them.  Black doesn't stand out, so it's not like it's highlighted.  I personally usually don't like white cables, even for all white builds, because the RGB highlights it, almost makes it glow, and I don't want the attention to be drawn to cables.
I've had great results with Dark Flash products, I like their CPU coolers also.
reviews.author: Minty

reviews.title: Great Bang for your Buck!
reviews.comment: This is a great case and is very compact! Only issue i have with it is the air flow options: it only has 5 120mm fan mounting options: 2top, 1rear, 2bottom. Which isnt great for optimal airflow as I have to have the top and rear as exhaust and the bottom 2 (bought separately) as the only intakes. Other than that one gripe its a great case for the price point for sure!
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: Quality case, rolled metal edge, good fans, super nice finish.
reviews.comment:
This has to be one of the best cases I've used.
I've been building computers for over 20 years, gaming systems for 10+.
Every metal edge is rolled, not a single sharp edge. The metal is thick and makes for a nice ridgid case. the glass is perfectly flat with no worbly effect. Fans are quiet, blow we'll, and are very crisp and bright.
Good choice of wire run ports,
The finish is excellent. Not just a spray over the outside, the whole chair is finished, not a single spot showing the metal underneath.
This build did not use an AIO, however there is plenty enough room, even in this mATX case to easily fit  one.
I went back to their store to see what other cases they have. Sadly my other two computers are we'll established and I can't justify just upgrading a case. But oh, how I want to
reviews.author: Carol L. Mccawley

reviews.title: Terrible airflow. Hugely disappointed
reviews.comment:
Terrible airflow.
Looks nice, but cannot house any modern CPUs.
9600X
5070
Idle temps are fine, around 40C, but during gaming the cpu jumps to a steady 75C with peaks at 82.
Has “flow holes” on the bottom, but nowhere for cool air to actually intake (power supply directly underneath one and a sealed cavity otherwise).
reviews.author: Chris
